1.a: Entities: Artist, Album, Song. Artist makes songs, Album contains songs. Genre maybe but not needed.
1.b: Artist: id, name. Album: id, name, year. Song: id, title, length. No foreign keys shown.
1.c: No recursive relationships because artists are independent.

2.a: Primary key is (O, L) from the given relation.
2.b: Deletion anomaly: deleting a record removes too much info. Insertion anomaly: can't add without all fields.
2.c: 3NF decomposition: R1(O,L), R2(L,M), R3(M,N). That removes anomalies.

3.a: Atomicity: all or nothing. Consistency: valid state. Isolation: transactions don't interfere. Durability: saved after commit.
3.b: Schedule S1 is conflict serializable. Schedule S2 is also conflict serializable. Both can be reordered.
3.c: 2PL means lock before read/write, unlock after transaction. T1 locks A then B. T2 locks B then A. Deadlock happens so DBMS must choose victim.

4.a: Q1: π name (σ title='DBMS' (Student ⋈ Enroll ⋈ Course)). Q2: π name (Student ⋈ (π sid,count(cid) (Enroll) ÷ π cid (Course))). Q3: π title (Course - π cid (Enroll)).
4.b: Q1: {s.name | Student(s) ∧ Enroll(e) ∧ Course(c) ∧ e.sid=s.sid ∧ c.title='DBMS'}. Q2 is hard. Q3: {c.title | Course(c) ∧ ¬∃e (e.cid=c.cid)}.

5.b: NoSQL types: key-value, document, graph. Mapping: tables become documents, rows become JSON objects, joins become nested objects.
